title: Step-up authentication and ZIdentity authentication levels

prose.text: Step-up authentication is a ZIdentity feature that ZIA policy can consume; the full ZIdentity treatment is in the legacy document [[doc:references/zidentity/step-up-authentication.md]]. "Authentication levels" in older ZIA screens and notes is the same feature under an older name.
How this layers on ZIA's own identity mechanisms (cookie, Kerberos, surrogate IP, covered from [[zia.authentication]]) is open {{gap:zia-layering}}.

checks.do: Whether the tenant uses an OIDC external IdP, since step-up is not available with Hosted DB or SAML alone.
Whether each authentication level is mapped to its acr value in the IdP.
Whether the failing rule sits in a policy that the step-up flow applies to.

what-it-is.statement: Step-up authentication prompts a user to re-authenticate at a higher assurance level, typically with MFA, when accessing a sensitive resource. It is configured with authentication levels that are hierarchical: higher levels are stronger, and a user authenticated at a higher level satisfies policies requiring a sub-level. The levels are mapped to access policies in supported Zscaler services.

quotes: Step-up authentication is a method that prompts users to reauthenticate with a higher assurance level (e.g., using MFA) when accessing specific resources.
These levels are hierarchical, where higher levels provide stronger assurance.
When users are authenticated at a higher level, their authentication level satisfies policies that require a sub-level of authentication.
These authentication levels are mapped with access policies in supported Zscaler services to enable step-up authentication for resources.

flow.statement: The flow is: the user logs in with standard credentials; on reaching a sensitive resource defined by Internet & SaaS (ZIA) or Private Access (ZPA) policy, the Authentication Service checks the required level; if the current level is insufficient it prompts re-authentication, typically MFA through Zscaler Client Connector; on success access is granted.

quotes: Authentication Service checks the required authentication level.
Authentication Service prompts the user to reauthenticate, typically using MFA via Zscaler Client Connector.

oidc-only.statement: Step-up authentication is supported only with OIDC-based external IdP integrations; when an external IdP is used via OIDC, each authentication level must be mapped to its acr value in the IdP.

quotes: Step-up authentication is supported only with OIDC-based external IdP integrations.
you need to map the authentication levels to their respective acr values in the IdP.

not-for-hosted-saml.statement: A tenant authenticating with Hosted DB or with SAML alone, without an OIDC external IdP, cannot use step-up authentication.
not-for-hosted-saml.conditions: Follows from the OIDC-only statement; no source names Hosted DB or SAML-only tenants.

level-limits.statement: Each level has a validity period in minutes, hours or days, and a parent level's validity must be less than that of any of its sub-levels. A tree of levels can hold at most 32 levels and no branch can be deeper than 4.

quotes: The validity period for a parent level must be less than the validity period defined for any of its sub-levels.
A tree can contain a total of up to 32 authentication levels and the maximum depth for any branch cannot exceed 4.
You can specify the validity period in minutes, hours, or days.

zia-layering.title: How ZIA's cookie and surrogate model combines with a ZIdentity level requirement
zia-layering.detail: Unverified legacy statement: ZIA enforces that the user is authenticated at all before any policy rule, then per-resource ZIA or ZPA rules can express a required ZIdentity level, triggering step-up if the current level is insufficient. No registered source states this. The step-up article confirms ZIA and ZPA policies can require a level; how that interacts with ZIA's cookie, Kerberos and surrogate identity is not stated. A lab rule requiring a level, hit by a cookie-less client, would settle it.
zia-layering.blocks: predicting what a cookie-less or surrogate-attributed request does when a rule requires a stronger level
